items.text: Counterexample: a morphism of ringed spaces that is not local

$V$ a discrete valuation ring (formal power series $k[[T]]$), $K=\operatorname{Frac}V$; $\operatorname{Spec}K=\{pt\}\to\operatorname{Spec}V$ sending the point to the closed point, with $V\hookrightarrow K$ on the stalk.
$V\to K$ is a ring homomorphism but not local; the morphism of ringed spaces does not come from a ring homomorphism (the map of spectra from $V\to K$ sends the point to the generic point).
Locality determines the map of spectra
\varphi\ \text{local}:\ \ f\notin\mathfrak q\iff u(f)\notin\mathfrak p\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \mathfrak q=u^{-1}(\mathfrak p),\ \ y=\varphi(x)
An affine $k$-scheme: a locally ringed space isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$, $A$ a $k$-algebra.
A scheme: a locally ringed space $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ with $X=\bigcup X_i$, each $X_i$ an affine scheme. A $k$-scheme: a ring homomorphism $k\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$.
X(k')=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}k',X)\qquad\text{(functor of points; morphisms of locally ringed spaces over }k)
To show: $X\mapsto X(-)$ is fully faithful from $k$-schemes to functors $k\text{-alg}\to\mathbf{Sets}$.
It remains to prove that the same diagram with primes (functors) is exact: $X'=\varinjlim X'_i$ in Zariski sheaves (not in functors), and $Y'$ is a sheaf.
